newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbek aircraft plant to sell 14 pct of its shares.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek aircraft plant to sell 14 pct of its shares.

text.p: Uzbekistan's Tashkent Aircraft Construction Factory, which produces Ilyushin cargo and passenger planes, has put up 14 percent of its shares for tender, the factory's head said on Wednesday.
"We plan to raise a total of 4.8 billion sums for the shares," Director General Vadim Kucherov told Reuters.
This is equivalent to 80.4 million dollars at the official exchange rate of 59.66 sums to the dollar. The blacket market exchange rate is around 140 sums to the dollar.
Kucherov said offers to buy the shares had been sent to a number of Russian and Uzbek commercial banks and to several aircraft factories in Russia.
Kucherov did not say whether Western investors would be allowed to take part in the tender, which is due to be completed by the end of the summer.
He said the 14 percent stake in the factory was offered at 10,000 sums per share, which is 10 times more than their face value.
The factory, based in the Uzbek capital Tashkent, was transformed into a joint-stock company in May last year. Its charter capital is 3.43 billion sums.

The state holds 51 percent of the factory's shares, with another 15 percent belonging to its workers. Uzbekistan's state-run Bank for Foreign Economic Activity and the Ministry of Foreign Economic Relations each hold 10-percent stakes.

Kucherov said the funds raised from the placement of the factory's 14 percent stake would be used to set up serial production of a new 64 seat passenger plane, the Ilyushin-114, and to modify Ilyushin-76 planes for heavy cargo.
